summary: This note is a wiki-style overview of the 2017–18 NBA season, the 72nd season of the National Basketball Association. It lists the season's dates, number of games and teams, TV partners, the top draft pick (Markelle Fultz to the Philadelphia 76ers), and the top seed and top scorer. The text also covers the season's opening game between the Cleveland Cavaliers and Boston Celtics, the Christmas and All-Star Game details, and the start and end of the playoffs and Finals; the note appears to combine several drafts of the same article, with some sentences written in the future tense and others in the past tense.
one_line: Overview of the 72nd NBA season (2017–18), covering its schedule, playoffs, Finals, draft pick, and All-Star Game.
key_facts: The 2017–18 NBA season was the 72nd season of the National Basketball Association (NBA).
The regular season began on October 17, 2017, with 82 games per team and 30 teams.
The 2017 Eastern Conference champion and Finals runner-up Cleveland Cavaliers hosted the Boston Celtics at Quicken Loans Arena in Cleveland, Ohio to open the season.
Christmas games were played on December 25, 2017.
The 2018 NBA All-Star Game was played on February 18, 2018, at the Staples Center in Los Angeles, California.
LeBron James of the Cleveland Cavaliers was named the All-Star Game Most Valuable Player.
The regular season ended on April 11, 2018, and the playoffs began on April 14, 2018.
The Finals were scheduled from May 31 to June 17, 2018.
The playoffs were listed as running April 14 to May 28, 2018.
The season's TV partners were ABC, TNT, ESPN, and NBA TV.
Markelle Fultz was the top draft pick, selected by the Philadelphia 76ers.
The Houston Rockets were the top seed in the regular season.
James Harden of the Houston Rockets was the top scorer.
The season was intended to begin earlier than previous seasons to reduce the number of back-to-back games teams were scheduled to play.
